content.text:
The £30 booking deposit isn't enough. The hirer must get prior written permission to serve alcohol and provide a separate £100 damage deposit, so **£130 in deposits altogether**.

- **Permission:** Alcohol may be served only with prior written permission (hall-conduct.md, 3.1). The hirer isn't selling the wine, which is consistent with 3.2: alcohol may not be sold under an ordinary hall booking.
- **Damage deposit:** Permission to serve alcohol requires the damage deposit (hall-conduct.md, 3.3). Parties serving alcohol need a £100 damage deposit (hall-fees.md, 5.2).
- **Booking deposit:** Every booking requires a £30 booking deposit (hall-fees.md, 5.1). The damage deposit is separate from it (hall-fees.md, 5.3), so the two add up to £130.

hall-changes.md doesn't replace any of these sections.
